newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland calling tender for DCS digital phone system.
newsitem.headline: Poland calling tender for DCS digital phone system.

text.p: Firms wanting to tender to build a new DCS 1800 digital telephone system in Poland will be able to collect documentation from next week and place offers in mid-July, public television said on Wednesday.

It reported Telecommunications Minister Andrzej Zielinski as saying the first such mobile telephones should be operating by the end of the year because investors would have to catch up with GSM systems already operating in Poland.

"The victor will probably try to invest in the initial stage of developing the network as fast as possible, as the passage of time will inevitably worsen its situation because GSM is already functioning," he said.

He said the DCS technology was suitable for cities and therefore the tender would be for serving cities of above 250,000 residents. Earlier tenders to run two new GSM digital telephone networks, which began operating last year, caused controversy because they were won by firms other than Ameritech and France Telecom, partners of the former state telecommunications firm, TPSA.

The foreign firms argued they had invested in the obsolete analogue Centertel system after being assured they would get a share in the GSM digital business. Ameritech sold its 24.5 percent stake in Centertel to its partners.
The director-general of PTK Centertel, Marek Jozefiak, confirmed at a news conference on Wednesday that his company would bid to build a mobile telephone network using the DCS 1800 digital system.

Centertel, which launched operations in Poland in 1991 and in which state firm TPSA has a 66 percent stake, still leads the market with more than 185,000 customers, but competitors Era GSM and GSM Plus are catching up.
